content.text:
Auth is in place using **WorkOS AuthKit**. Build, typecheck and lint pass. With placeholder credentials, `/` loads, and `/dashboard`, `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` all redirect to WorkOS's hosted sign-in page. I couldn't test a real sign-in end to end, because that needs real WorkOS credentials.

**Why WorkOS:** WorkOS hosts the sign-in and sign-up pages, so email + password and Google work without building any forms. Sessions are stored in an encrypted cookie, so no database is needed. That fits, because Notely's users only live in memory right now. It also supports Next 16's `proxy.ts`, and a repo-local copy of its docs was already in `docs/`. I checked the guide against the installed package (v4.6.2) instead of trusting it as written.

**What changed**
- **`src/lib/users.ts`**: `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session and returns `undefined` for signed-out visitors. The new `requireUser()` sends signed-out visitors to sign in. On sign-in, the WorkOS account is linked to a local user by WorkOS ID, then by email, so Ada and Grace keep their records. Anyone new gets a user record created. `User` gains an optional `workosId`.
- **`/dashboard` is protected twice**:
  - `src/proxy.ts` blocks signed-out requests before the page runs (only `/` is public).
  - The page itself calls `requireUser()`. It also has a Sign out button now, and the "nobody" fallback is gone.
- **New routes**: `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, and `/auth/callback`, which sends you to `/dashboard` after signing in.
- **Home page**: the Create Next App placeholder is replaced with a small Notely page showing Sign in / Sign up, or a link to the dashboard if you're signed in. The page title is now "Notely".
- **`.env.example`**: holds the four placeholder variables. I also added `!.env.example` to `.gitignore`, because the existing `.env*` rule would have kept it out of git.

**To make it work for real, in the WorkOS dashboard:**
1. Turn on Email + Password and Google OAuth under Authentication.
2. Add `http://localhost:3000/auth/callback` as a redirect URI.
3. Set a default Sign-out URI, such as `http://localhost:3000/`. Sign out redirects there.
4. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in your real values. Generate the cookie password with `openssl rand -base64 32`.

**Limitation:** because the user store is still in memory, users created on first sign-in disappear when the server restarts. Their WorkOS accounts stay; the local record is simply recreated at their next sign-in. A real database would fix this.

Nothing is committed.
